messages.text: I’ll audit the combined integration’s physical handoffs and payload accounting at the pinned revision, then pass any concrete traps to the implementation agent.

The current combined exporter still builds the legacy short-strip components. Its service reconciler only combines trunks with identical radial and angular bounds, so the new corridor needs a deliberate replacement path. I’m checking how feeds, optical groups and cooling circuits join along z to prevent gaps or double counting.

**DES043 integration audit completed at `2c1bfe02e87f201abcd1e461a554d951bdc7f56e`.** The proposed handoffs are coherent with explicit replacement and partitioning of legacy services. Critical traps were sent to SoftEng, who confirmed the intended approach.

- **Replace legacy short-strip collector/trunk/fan cells and walls.** The new fan, r690..781.5 and local w20..100 mm, overlaps the new r717..781.5 trunk. Partition that space and retain one carrier; placing complete fans over an unbroken trunk would double count solids and payload. Existing reconciliation only merges identical bounds and matches top-level trunk names (`tracker_dd4hep/services.py:18–33`).
- **Join at disc z+100 mm.** Current `short_strip_redesign/model.py:124` retains +85 for route-length accounting, while `diagnostics.py:123` uses +100. The difference represents 6.48 power-bundle metres globally; distinguish that conservative ledger reservation from actual integrated placement.
- **Keep the existing long-strip ownership rule.** Remove the standalone long-barrel trunk while retaining the cumulative DES-023 barrel-plus-endcap services (`services.py:21–24`).

Independent endpoint arithmetic gives:

| Quantity | Per end | Both ends |
|---|---:|---:|
| Power bundles | 504 | 1,008 |
| Optical groups | 792 | 1,584 |
| Local cooling circuits | 432 | 864 |
| Final bulk pipe pairs | 68 | 136 |
| Physical end boards | 360 | 720 |

Barrel sector populations are `[25,25,22]` repeated four times. After n endcap stations, each sector requires `B+3n` power bundles, `2B+3n` optical groups and `ceil(B/8)+ceil(2n/8)` bulk pairs. The final worst sector is **43/68/6**, reproducing the **0.961844** adverse area utilization (`model.py:95–108`).

Conserve the **new** designed constituent inventory through cell partitioning. Per 8 mm power envelope, the conservative allocation is **25.22 mm² Cu, 15.027289 mm² PI and 10.018193 mm² internal air**. The Cu value reserves HV capacity for 14 modules; an actual 11-module endcap island uses 24.38 mm². Packing/spare factors affect capacity checks, not material quantities. Count unused corridor air separately once.

Two further integration requirements remain:

- Barrel inserts need actual backing/front-skin/glue/core windows and **straight plus U-torus pipe cuts**. Central lands extend below the straight-leg start. Their host-frame bounds are w−4.05..lift−0.825; centres must be u±12, replacing old ±10 (`short_strip_barrel/export.py:105–125,167–169`).
- Use all twelve redesigned discs, standard readout names and system translation 4→5. The isolated native export defaults to only 792 sensors; combined integration requires **4,752 endcap sensors**, plus 8,064 barrel sensors.

**Mass-validation trap:** `tracker_dd4hep/validate.py:39` subtracts complete cutter capacities. That is invalid for intersecting/outside DES043 window and saddle cuts. Native entities also deliberately omit exact CSG volumes. Keep such volumes explicitly bounded or unsupported until independently audited; construction, identifiers, overlaps and contact probes can be validated separately.

Actual checks: pinned-source inspection and independent stdlib count/constituent/packing calculations. **No files changed; no native jobs run; no engineering acceptance claimed.**
